svg.title: Ghettoisation in Poland & Operation Barbarossa: “Holocaust by Bullets” (1939–42)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 9 historical GIS atlas map of Eastern Central Europe (1939–1942) showing German-occupied Poland and major sealed ghettos (Warsaw, Łódź, Kraków, Lublin), the 22 June 1941 Operation Barbarossa launch line, Einsatzgruppen A, B, C, and D mobile killing squad advances across the Baltic States, Belarus, and Ukraine, mass-shooting sites at Kaunas, Ponary Forest (Vilna), Rumbula, Maly Trostenets, and Babi Yar (Kyiv), and the first stationary gas-van camp at Chełmno (December 1941).

text.tspan: Over 400,000 walled into Warsaw after Heydrich’s order
Invasion of USSR begins war of annihilation
Einsatzgruppe A & local auxiliaries murder tens of thousands
Einsatzgruppe C & Order Police murder 33,771 in two days
First stationary killing site using mobile gas vans

g.text: SS Einsatzgruppen A, B, C & D Killing Squad Routes
Major Sealed Ghetto (Warsaw, Łódź, Kraków, Lublin)
Major Mass-Shooting Ravine / Forest Murder Site

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: THE SHOAH
Ghettoisation in Poland & Operation Barbarossa: “Holocaust by Bullets” (1939–42)
From 1939, Nazi Germany walled Polish Jews into starving urban ghettos; after 22 June 1941, Barbarossa turned conquest into mass murder.
Over 1.5 million Jews were shot in pits & ravines like Ponary and Babi Yar before Chełmno (Dec 1941) began stationary poison-gas killing.
